bessemer-and-the-price-of-steel.alt: Wood engraving of an upright fixed converter in a works, sparks jetting sideways from openings in its side, workmen with rods below and top-hatted visitors watching, with sectional diagrams inset at the corners.
bessemer-and-the-price-of-steel.caption: The converter as German readers first met it, in the 1856 Gartenlaube article "Bessemer's Eisenfegfeuer", sparks blowing from the vessel's side while the workmen judge the blow by eye.
bessemer-and-the-price-of-steel.creator: Unknown artist, via Wikimedia Commons

haber-bosch-and-the-bread-from-air.alt: Sepia photograph of a long row of tall cylindrical absorption towers at an early 20th-century German chemical works, linked by pipe bridges, ladders and an overhead gantry crane.
haber-bosch-and-the-bread-from-air.caption: The absorption towers of the nitric acid plant at BASF's Oppau works near Ludwigshafen — the site where Haber-Bosch ammonia first went into industrial-scale production — photographed between about 1910 and the works' destruction in the explosion of 21 September 1921.
haber-bosch-and-the-bread-from-air.creator: A. Gross, Berlin — credited on the object itself as both photographer and publisher (Illustrations-Verlag, Berlin SW68). The Commons \"Author\" field names the Rijksmuseum, which is the holding/source institution rather than the creator., via Wikimedia Commons

harrison-and-the-longitude-problem.alt: An engraving of a three-masted warship flying the royal standard driving onto jagged rocks in heavy seas, with a dismasted vessel and men in the water to the right and other ships of the squadron standing offshore.
harrison-and-the-longitude-problem.caption: A print of about 1710 showing Sir Cloudesley Shovell's flagship Association striking the Western Rocks of Scilly on 22 October 1707.
harrison-and-the-longitude-problem.creator: Unknown engraver, via Wikimedia Commons

tacoma-narrows-and-the-flutter-problem.alt: Black-and-white film frame of the Tacoma Narrows Bridge deck twisted steeply about its centreline, suspender cables splayed at sharp angles, an abandoned car canted against the raised edge of the tilted roadway.
tacoma-narrows-and-the-flutter-problem.caption: A frame from Professor F. B. Farquharson's 16 mm film of 7 November 1940, copied for the Historic American Engineering Record.
tacoma-narrows-and-the-flutter-problem.creator: F. B. Farquharson / Historic American Engineering Record, via Wikimedia Commons

the-antikythera-mechanism.alt: Three green corroded bronze fragments of the Antikythera mechanism mounted on clear perspex stands inside a glass museum case, the central piece dominated by a large four-spoked gear wheel.
the-antikythera-mechanism.caption: Fragments of the Antikythera mechanism in the National Archaeological Museum, Athens, with the four-spoked main drive wheel of Fragment A at the centre.
the-antikythera-mechanism.creator: Joyofmuseums, via Wikimedia Commons

the-apollo-guidance-computer.alt: A gold-anodised rectangular Apollo Guidance Computer chassis rests on a pale blue background beside its DSKY unit, which shows a numeric keypad, VERB and NOUN keys, dark register windows and status lamps including RESTART and GIMBAL LOCK.
the-apollo-guidance-computer.caption: The Apollo Guidance Computer chassis and its display-and-keyboard unit, the DSKY, whose status panel included a lamp marked simply RESTART.
the-apollo-guidance-computer.creator: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons

the-discovery-of-insulin.alt: Sepia photograph of two men in three-piece suits seated before a bookcase; a younger clean-shaven man at left with hands clasped, and an older man in round wire-rimmed spectacles at right.
the-discovery-of-insulin.caption: Charles Best, left, and Frederick Banting photographed around 1924, two years after the first insulin injections at Toronto General Hospital.
the-discovery-of-insulin.creator: Unknown photographer (University of Toronto Libraries), via Wikimedia Commons

the-jacquard-loom-and-the-punched-card.alt: An 1839 silk portrait woven on a Jacquard loom shows Jacquard seated in his workshop holding dividers, with a fan of punched cards and a small loom model on the table beside him.
the-jacquard-loom-and-the-punched-card.caption: \"À la mémoire de J.M. Jacquard\" (Didier, Petit et Cie, Lyon, 1839) is not a print but a portrait woven in silk on a Jacquard loom from roughly 24,000 punched cards, after Claude Bonnefond's painting.
the-jacquard-loom-and-the-punched-card.creator: Woven in silk by Michel-Marie Carquillat (1803–1884) for Didier, Petit et Cie, Lyon, after the painting by Claude Bonnefond (1796–1860). Commons author field reads: \"Bonnefond, Claude, 1796-1860, artist; Carquillat, François Michel-Marie, 1803-1884.\" Woven at the bottom of the object: \"Tissé par M.M. Carquillat.\", via Wikimedia Commons

the-ozone-hole-and-the-montreal-protocol.alt: A false-colour satellite map of total ozone over the South Pole, a large blue and purple region of very low ozone covering Antarctica, ringed by green, yellow and red bands of thicker ozone.
the-ozone-hole-and-the-montreal-protocol.caption: NASA's total column ozone map for 1 October 1998, with blue and purple marking the depleted air inside the springtime Antarctic ozone hole.
the-ozone-hole-and-the-montreal-protocol.creator: NASA, via Wikimedia Commons

the-quantum-revolution.alt: Twenty-nine physicists in formal dark suits posed in three rows outside a stone building; Albert Einstein sits at the centre of the front row, Marie Curie seated third from left.
the-quantum-revolution.caption: The fifth Solvay Conference, Brussels, October 1927 — where Bohr and Einstein argued over the new quantum mechanics — photographed by Benjamin Couprie.
the-quantum-revolution.creator: Benjamin Couprie (1875–1962), Institut International de Physique Solvay, Brussels, via Wikimedia Commons

the-rise-of-germ-theory.alt: Detailed 1854 street map of Soho, London, printed in black and white, with stacked black bars marking cholera deaths clustered densely around the Broad Street water pump.
the-rise-of-germ-theory.caption: John Snow's 1854 map of Soho: every short black bar is a cholera death, and the bars pile up around the Broad Street pump.
the-rise-of-germ-theory.creator: John Snow (1813–1858); lithographed and printed by C. F. Cheffins, Lith., Southampton Buildings, London, via Wikimedia Commons

the-transatlantic-cable.alt: Watercolour of the large iron steamship Great Eastern at sea under a cloudy sky, flags at her masts, smaller escort ships behind her, and a red-jacketed figure in a boat on the green swell.
the-transatlantic-cable.caption: The cable fleet at sea in 1865: Robert Dudley's watercolour of the Great Eastern under way with her escorts, painted by the expedition's own official artist aboard the ship.
the-transatlantic-cable.creator: Robert Charles Dudley (British, 1826–1909), via Wikimedia Commons

the-transistor-at-bell-labs.alt: Black-and-white laboratory photograph of three men in shirtsleeves and neckties at a bench strewn with wiring, one seated at centre behind a small microscope and looking up, two standing and leaning in, a rack of dials at left.
the-transistor-at-bell-labs.caption: A staged Bell Labs publicity photograph of John Bardeen, William Shockley and Walter Brattain, from the series issued around the 1948 announcement of the transistor.
the-transistor-at-bell-labs.creator: AT&T, via Wikimedia Commons
